questions.title: Transmission with change in form but no multiplication
questions.question: The organism undergoes cyclical changes, but it does not multiply inside the arthropod. This is called ...... transmission.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Transporting (mechanical) transmission means the arthropod merely carries the organism on its body surface or in its gut without the organism developing or multiplying at all, the way a housefly carries bacteria on contaminated legs. Here the organism undergoes cyclical (developmental) changes, which mechanical transmission does not involve.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Trans-ovarian transmission describes passage of the organism from an infected female arthropod to her own offspring through the egg, a route seen with some tick-borne pathogens. It is defined by the generational route of passage, not by whether the organism changes form without multiplying inside a single host arthropod.
explanations.C: Correct. Cyclodevelopmental transmission describes a parasite that undergoes a morphological or developmental change inside the vector but does not increase in number there — exactly the pattern described, cyclical changes without multiplication. This is the pattern seen, for example, with microfilariae developing into infective larvae inside a mosquito.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cyclo-propagative transmission requires the organism to both change form and multiply inside the vector, as Plasmodium does during sporogony in Anopheles. The stem explicitly excludes multiplication, ruling this option out.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Propagative transmission means the organism simply increases in number inside the vector without any change in form, as Yersinia pestis does inside a flea. The stem describes cyclical (developmental) change, not simple multiplication, so propagative does not fit.

questions.learning_objective: Identify cyclodevelopmental transmission as development without multiplication inside the vector.

questions.title: Gravid segments of pseudophyllidean cestodes
questions.question: Regarding the gravid segments of pseudophyllidea, which of the following is true?

options.C: They can be detected in stool.
options.D: They can be considered as diagnostic stages.

explanations.A: Correct. Pseudophyllidean cestodes such as Diphyllobothrium latum do not shed discrete gravid proglottids the way cyclophyllidean tapeworms do. Instead their uterus opens directly onto the segment surface through a uterine pore, releasing operculated eggs continuously into the lumen rather than releasing whole detached gravid segments. True gravid segments are therefore absent from this life cycle.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Mature genital organs are a feature of proglottids generally, including the mature (not gravid) segments of pseudophyllideans, but since discrete gravid segments are not shed at all in this order, describing 'their' contents is not the relevant distinguishing fact tested here.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Because gravid segments are not shed, it is operculated eggs — not segments — that are detected in stool examination for pseudophyllidean infection, which is precisely the opposite of what this option claims.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Since gravid segments are absent in this order, they cannot serve as a diagnostic stage; the diagnostic stage for pseudophyllidean infection is instead the operculated egg passed directly through the uterine pore.
explanations.E: Incorrect. 'Broader than longer' describes the shape of gravid proglottids in some cyclophyllidean tapeworms (such as Taenia saginata's segments, which are longer than broad, in contrast to some others), not a feature of pseudophyllidean biology, where discrete gravid segments do not occur in the first place.

questions.learning_objective: State that pseudophyllidean cestodes do not shed discrete gravid proglottids.

questions.title: Organism passing undigested through the intestine
questions.question: Foreign organism that passes through the human intestine without causing any disease, is a/an ...... parasite.

explanations.A: Correct. A coprozoic organism is a free-living species that passes through the alimentary tract undigested, appearing in a stool sample as an artefact of examination rather than as evidence of true infection. Exactly the scenario described, a foreign organism transiting the intestine without causing disease.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An opportunistic pathogen is normally harmless or low-virulence but causes disease specifically when host defences are impaired (for example in immunosuppression), which is the opposite of an organism that passes through causing no disease under any circumstance being described here.
explanations.C: Incorrect. 'Nonspecific' is not a recognised parasitological term for this scenario; it does not describe a defined category of organism found in stool examination the way coprozoic, opportunistic or facultative do.
explanations.D: Incorrect. An endoparasite lives inside its host and, by definition as a parasite, causes some degree of harm or draws nutrition at the host's expense; the organism described here causes no disease at all and is not actually infecting the host, so it does not qualify as an endoparasite.
explanations.E: Incorrect. A facultative parasite is one capable of both a free-living and a parasitic existence, actually establishing infection when it does behave parasitically. The organism in this stem never infects the host at all, which is a coprozoic (transient, non-infecting) finding rather than facultative parasitism.

questions.learning_objective: Define a coprozoic organism as a free-living species passing through the gut undigested, causing no disease.

questions.title: Yellow fever vector
questions.question: Yellow fever virus is transmitted by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Culex mosquitoes transmit diseases such as bird (avian) malaria, Japanese encephalitis and (with Aedes) Rift Valley fever, but not yellow fever, which is transmitted by a different mosquito genus.
explanations.B: Correct. Aedes mosquitoes, particularly Aedes aegypti, are the vector of yellow fever, a viral haemorrhagic fever. The same genus also transmits dengue, chikungunya and Zika virus.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Anopheles mosquitoes are the exclusive vector of human malaria, completing the sexual (sporogonic) cycle of Plasmodium species; they are not the vector for yellow fever.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sand flies transmit Leishmania species (leishmaniasis) and sandfly fever virus, not yellow fever, which requires a mosquito vector rather than a sand fly.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Fleas transmit organisms such as Yersinia pestis (plague) and some cestodes (Dipylidium caninum, Hymenolepis diminuta), not arboviruses like yellow fever, which requires a mosquito vector to complete its transmission cycle.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Aedes as the mosquito vector of yellow fever.

questions.title: Host harbouring larvae without further development
questions.question: A host which harbours the larval stage of the parasite without further development is a/an ...... host.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The intermediate host is where the parasite's larval stages actively develop further, progressing toward the next infective stage — the opposite of the arrested-development scenario the stem describes.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The definitive (final) host harbours the parasite's adult or sexually reproducing stage, not an arrested larval stage being merely carried onward.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A vector is an arthropod that actively transmits a parasite or pathogen between hosts, often supporting some part of its development or multiplication; the stem instead describes a host in which no further development occurs at all.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A reservoir host is a non-human animal harbouring the same parasite species that infects humans, serving as an additional source of human infection — a role defined by being an alternative source of infection, not by arrested larval development.
explanations.E: Correct. A paratenic (transfer) host harbours the parasite in an arrested state of development. No further maturation happens there, but the host carries the organism onward until it reaches a host in which development can resume or the definitive host is reached, exactly the scenario in the stem.

questions.subtopic: Host types in the parasite life cycle
questions.learning_objective: Identify the paratenic (transfer) host as one that carries larvae without further development.

questions.title: Parasite able to exist independently
questions.question: Parasite which lives upon another organism but can exist independently, is a/an ...... parasite.

explanations.A: Incorrect. An accidental parasite infects a host it does not normally infect (an unusual or coincidental host), a description about which host is involved, not about whether the organism can also live independently of any host.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An obligatory parasite must spend all or an essential part of its life cycle within a host to survive and cannot live independently — the direct opposite of a parasite that 'can exist independently', which the stem describes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. An endoparasite is simply one that lives inside the host's body (as opposed to on its surface); this describes location, not whether the organism is capable of an independent, free-living existence.
explanations.D: Correct. A facultative parasite can alternate between a free-living and a parasitic mode of life. It lives upon (or within) another organism but is also capable of surviving independently, which exactly matches the stem's description.

questions.learning_objective: Identify a facultative parasite as one able to live either parasitically or independently.

questions.title: Nematode digestive system
questions.question: Regarding the digestive system of nematoda, which of the following is true?

options.A: Oesophagus has same shape and structure
options.B: Mouth provided with the lips, teeth, plates and sensory papillae.
options.C: Starting with mouth and Intestinal caeca end blindly (no anus).
options.D: Mouth at the anterior portion surrounded by oral sucker

explanations.A: Incorrect. The nematode oesophagus is muscular, but its exact shape and structure vary between species (club-shaped, cylindrical or with a posterior bulb, depending on the genus) rather than being identical across all nematodes, so this generalisation is not accurate.
explanations.B: Correct. The nematode mouth is provided with accessory structures. Lips, teeth or cutting plates depending on the species — together with sensory papillae used to detect food and environmental cues, which is a defining general character of nematode anatomy.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Nematodes possess a complete digestive tract running from an anterior mouth to a posterior anus; describing the gut as ending blindly with no anus is instead a feature of cestodes, which have no digestive tract at all, not of nematodes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A mouth surrounded by an oral sucker is a trematode (fluke) feature, not a nematode one; the nematode mouth instead bears lips, teeth or plates as described in the correct option.

questions.learning_objective: Describe the nematode mouth as bearing lips, teeth or plates and sensory papillae.

questions.title: Relationship where one benefits and the host is unharmed
questions.question: it is a relationship between two living organisms where one benefits, while the other (host) is not harmed.

explanations.A: Incorrect. In mutualism both partners benefit from the relationship; the stem specifies that only one organism benefits while the other is merely unharmed, not itself gaining anything, which does not fit mutualism.
explanations.B: Correct. Commensalism is a relationship in which one organism benefits while the host is neither helped nor harmed. Precisely the relationship the stem describes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. In parasitism the parasite benefits at the direct expense of the host, which is harmed; the stem explicitly states the host is not harmed, ruling out parasitism.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Symbiosis is a broad umbrella term for organisms living together in close association, encompassing mutualism, commensalism and parasitism as its subtypes; it is not itself the specific 'one benefits, host unharmed' relationship being asked for.

questions.learning_objective: Define commensalism as a relationship in which one organism benefits and the host is unharmed.

questions.title: Human malaria vector
questions.question: Human malaria transmitted by

explanations.A: Correct. Anopheles mosquitoes are the exclusive vector of human malaria. The female mosquito injects Plasmodium sporozoites into the bloodstream during a blood meal, completing the sporogonic cycle that only this genus among mosquitoes supports for the four human Plasmodium species. No other mosquito genus can complete this sexual cycle of the parasite.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Culex mosquitoes transmit diseases such as bird (avian) malaria, Japanese encephalitis and Rift Valley fever, not human malaria, which requires Anopheles specifically.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Aedes mosquitoes transmit yellow fever, dengue, chikungunya and Zika virus; they do not support the Plasmodium sporogonic cycle required for human malaria transmission.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Musca (the housefly) is a mechanical vector that carries pathogens passively on its body surface or in its gut without supporting any biological development; it plays no role in malaria transmission, which requires the Anopheles mosquito as a biological vector.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Anopheles as the exclusive vector of human malaria.

questions.title: True statement about nematode anatomy
questions.question: Regarding the nematoda, which of the following is true?

options.C: Oesophagus is in the muscular shape and structure.
options.D: Few vitelline glands in the posterior third on both sides.
options.E: The body is generally flattened, leaf-like and segmented.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Nematodes reproduce sexually, with separate male and female worms mating, rather than reproducing asexually; 'multiplies asexually' does not describe standard nematode reproduction.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An oral opening surrounded by suckers describes trematodes, not nematodes; the nematode mouth instead bears lips, teeth or cutting plates.
explanations.C: Correct. The nematode oesophagus (pharynx) is muscular in shape and structure. It pumps ingested material into the intestine, working against the pressure of the worm's own pseudocoelomic fluid. This muscular oesophagus is one of the defining general anatomical characters used to identify nematodes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Vitelline glands producing yolk for the eggs are a feature of trematode (and to some extent cestode) reproductive anatomy, not of nematodes, which have a different reproductive tract structure entirely.
explanations.E: Incorrect. A generally flattened, leaf-like and segmented body describes trematodes (flatworms), not nematodes, which are unsegmented, cylindrical (round) worms — a feature reflected in the common name roundworm.

questions.learning_objective: State that the nematode oesophagus is muscular in shape and structure.

questions.title: General characters of trematodes
questions.question: Regarding general characters of the trematodes, choose the correct answer:

options.D: Male organs ended by simple spicules.
options.E: The body is generally flattened, leaf-like and segmented

explanations.A: Incorrect. Most trematodes have a single genital pore, but describing it as specifically 'unilateral' is not the general defining character being tested; the mouth's oral sucker is the classic general character of the group.
explanations.B: Correct. Trematodes (flukes) have a mouth surrounded by an oral sucker, used for attachment and feeding, with most species also carrying a second, ventral (acetabular) sucker further along the body. A defining general character of the group.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Trematodes typically have a single set of female reproductive organs (one ovary), not two; having two full sets of female organs is not a standard trematode general character.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Male organs ending in spicules is a nematode feature (used to hold the female's vulva open during mating), not a trematode one; trematode male organs instead include testes with a cirrus for sperm transfer.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Trematodes are flattened and leaf-like but are not segmented; a flattened, leaf-like AND segmented body is not an accurate general description of trematode anatomy, since segmentation instead describes cestodes.

questions.learning_objective: Identify an oral sucker surrounding the mouth as a general character of trematodes.

questions.title: Chemical control of adult mosquitoes
questions.question: Chemical methods used for control of mosquitoes adult stages including:

options.B: Apply wire screening in doors and windows.
options.C: Citronella oil repellants applied on the skin.
options.D: Paris green spray on the water surface.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Malathion and diptrex are organophosphate insecticides more typically applied as residual sprays targeting resting or breeding-site mosquitoes rather than as the direct adult-stage repellent measure being tested here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Wire screening in doors and windows is a physical/mechanical barrier method, excluding adult mosquitoes without any chemical action, so it does not fit a question specifically asking for a chemical method.
explanations.C: Correct. Citronella oil repellents applied directly to the skin are a chemical method aimed specifically at deterring the adult (flying, biting) mosquito. This distinguishes the option from chemical measures aimed at the aquatic larval stage, such as larvicidal oils. It also distinguishes it from purely physical/mechanical barriers such as wire screening, which exclude adults without any chemical action.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Paris green sprayed on the water surface is a chemical larvicide, acting on the aquatic larval stage of the mosquito, not on the adult stage that the stem specifically asks about.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Sterilisation of males using irradiation is a genetic (sterile insect technique) control method; describing sterilisation as achieved 'using carbamates' conflates a genetic method with an unrelated insecticide class and is not an accurate chemical adult-control method.

questions.learning_objective: Identify skin-applied chemical repellents as a method of adult mosquito control.

questions.title: Conjugation reproduction in protozoa
questions.question: Regarding the conjugation reproduction of the protozoa, choose the right statement:

options.A: Occur by small division of the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
options.B: By formation of male and female gametes.
options.C: Occur by exchange of nuclear material between two organisms.
options.D: The organism produced several parts of small daughter cells.
options.E: Occur by formation of hemolysins and cytolysins.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Small division of the nucleus and cytoplasm into two describes binary fission, an asexual reproductive mode, not conjugation, which is a sexual process involving two separate organisms.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Formation and fusion of separate male and female gametes describes syngamy/gametogony, a different sexual reproductive mode (seen for example in the sexual cycle of Plasmodium in the mosquito), not conjugation.
explanations.C: Correct. Conjugation is a form of sexual reproduction in which two protozoal organisms temporarily join and exchange nuclear (genetic) material before separating, each then continuing to reproduce asexually. Exactly the process described.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Producing several small daughter cells at once from one organism describes multiple fission (schizogony), an asexual process, not the two-organism nuclear exchange that defines conjugation.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Hemolysins and cytolysins are virulence factors that damage host cells, unrelated to any mode of protozoal reproduction; this option does not describe a reproductive process at all.

questions.learning_objective: Define conjugation in protozoa as exchange of nuclear material between two organisms.

questions.title: Yellow fever vector (Final 38)
questions.question: Yellow fever is transmitted by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Anopheles mosquitoes are the exclusive vector of human malaria, not yellow fever, which requires the Aedes genus.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Culex mosquitoes transmit bird malaria, Japanese encephalitis and (with Aedes) Rift Valley fever, not yellow fever specifically.
explanations.C: Correct. Aedes mosquitoes, particularly Aedes aegypti, are the vector of yellow fever, transmitting the virus during a blood meal. The same genus also transmits dengue, chikungunya and Zika.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Lice transmit organisms such as Rickettsia prowazekii (epidemic typhus) and Borrelia recurrentis (louse-borne relapsing fever), not arboviruses like yellow fever, which requires a mosquito vector.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Fleas transmit Yersinia pestis (plague) and some cestodes, not yellow fever virus, which is transmitted exclusively by mosquitoes of the Aedes genus.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Aedes as the mosquito vector of yellow fever.

questions.title: Host harbouring larval immature reproducing forms
questions.question: The host which harbours larval immature stage (non-sexually) reproducing forms of the parasites called:

explanations.A: Incorrect. A paratenic host carries the parasite in an arrested state of development, with no further maturation or reproduction occurring there, which is the opposite of the actively reproducing larval forms the stem describes.
explanations.B: Correct. The intermediate host is where all of the parasite's larval developmental stages take place, including asexual (non-sexual) reproduction of immature forms, before the parasite becomes infective for the next host. Exactly matching the stem.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A reservoir host is a non-human animal harbouring the same parasite species that infects humans, serving as an additional source of infection; this role is defined by being an alternative infection source, not by hosting non-sexually reproducing larval stages.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The definitive (final) host harbours the parasite's adult or sexual reproductive stage, not the non-sexually reproducing immature/larval forms described in the stem.
explanations.E: Incorrect. 'Transport host' is essentially synonymous with the paratenic host, carrying the organism onward without further development — again the opposite of the actively developing/reproducing larval forms described here.

questions.subtopic: Host types in the parasite life cycle
questions.learning_objective: Identify the intermediate host as the site of non-sexually reproducing larval development.

questions.title: Cyclophyllidean cestode life cycle
questions.question: Regarding Cyclophyllidea, choose the right statement:

options.B: The body is cylindrical with tapering ends and separate sex.
options.C: It has elongated Rostellum with hooks.
options.D: Larva stage of procercoid present in the 1st intermediate host.
options.E: It has non operculated eggs with mature miracidium.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Blindly-ending intestinal caeca describe nematode gut anatomy (part of a complete but single-opening digestive arrangement in some contexts), not cyclophyllidean cestode biology; cestodes in fact have no digestive tract at all.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A cylindrical body with tapering ends and separate sexes describes nematodes (roundworms), not cyclophyllidean cestodes, which are flattened, segmented (ribbon-like) and typically hermaphroditic per proglottid.
explanations.C: Incorrect. While many cyclophyllidean genera do have an armed rostellum with hooks on the scolex, this is not a universal feature of the whole order (some genera are unarmed), and it is not the life-cycle fact the correct option specifically tests.
explanations.D: Correct. In cyclophyllidean cestodes with an indirect life cycle, the oncosphere released from an ingested egg develops into a procercoid-type larval stage within the first intermediate host. This larva then develops further, for example into a cysticercoid or cysticercus, in a second intermediate host or the same host depending on the species. Tracking which larval stage belongs to which intermediate host is a core part of understanding cestode life cycles.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Cyclophyllidean eggs are non-operculated but contain a mature oncosphere (hexacanth embryo), not a miracidium — a miracidium is the larval stage found inside trematode (fluke) eggs, not cestode eggs.

questions.learning_objective: State that cyclophyllidean cestodes develop a procercoid-type larva in the first intermediate host.

questions.title: Arthropod-transmitted spirochetal disease
questions.question: Which ONE of the following Spirochetal diseases is transmitted by an arthropod?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Leptospirosis is transmitted through contact with water or soil contaminated by the urine of infected animals, not by an arthropod vector.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Pinta is a non-venereal treponematosis spread by direct skin-to-skin contact with an infectious lesion, not by an arthropod.
explanations.C: Correct. Relapsing fever, caused by Borrelia species, is transmitted by an arthropod vector. The human body louse (epidemic relapsing fever) or soft ticks of the genus Ornithodoros (endemic relapsing fever) — making it the spirochetal disease among these options that requires an arthropod vector.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Yaws, like pinta, is a non-venereal treponematosis spread by direct contact with skin lesions, not by an arthropod vector.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Syphilis is transmitted sexually (or congenitally from mother to fetus), not through an arthropod vector.

questions.learning_objective: Identify relapsing fever as the spirochetal disease transmitted by an arthropod vector.

questions.title: Protozoal movement by gliding
questions.question: Which of the following parasites move by gliding?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Amoebae move by extending pseudopodia (amoeboid movement), not by gliding.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Flagellates move using one or more whip-like flagella (flagellar movement), a distinct mode of locomotion from gliding.
explanations.C: Correct. Sporozoa (apicomplexan protozoa such as Plasmodium and Toxoplasma) lack flagella, cilia or pseudopodia. Instead they move by gliding motility, a distinctive substrate-dependent locomotion powered by an internal actin-myosin motor beneath the cell membrane. This gliding motility is also essential for the organism's ability to invade host cells.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cestodes (tapeworms) are non-motile, sessile helminths attached to the host intestinal wall by a scolex; they do not have an active mode of independent locomotion such as gliding.

questions.learning_objective: Identify gliding as the characteristic mode of movement of sporozoa.

field_notes.relettered: source options printed a,b,d,e (skipping c); relettered A-D in sequence, correct answer (Sporozoa) kept as the third option.

questions.title: Cyclops transmitting D. latum
questions.question: By which type of disease transmission does cyclops transmit D. latum?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Propagative transmission means the organism multiplies inside the vector without changing form; in the cyclops, the coracidium develops into a procercoid without any multiplication in number, so propagative does not fit.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cyclopropagative transmission requires both multiplication and a change in form inside the vector; the coracidium-to-procercoid development inside the cyclops involves a change in form but no multiplication.
explanations.C: Correct. Inside the cyclops (the first intermediate host of Diphyllobothrium latum), the ingested coracidium develops into a procercoid larva. A change in form without any multiplication in number — which is exactly cyclodevelopmental transmission.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Transovarian transmission describes passage of an organism to an arthropod's own offspring through the egg; it does not describe the coracidium-to-procercoid developmental step happening within the cyclops itself.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Transporting (mechanical) transmission means the vector merely carries the organism without any development taking place; here, the parasite actively develops from one larval form to the next inside the cyclops, which mechanical transmission does not involve.

questions.learning_objective: Apply cyclodevelopmental transmission to the coracidium-to-procercoid step of D. latum inside the cyclops.

questions.title: Organisms with articulated appendages
questions.question: Which of the following have articulated appendages?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Amoebae are single-celled protozoa with no appendages at all; they move by extending pseudopodia, not by any jointed limb.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Flagellates are single-celled protozoa that move using flagella, a whip-like structure, not a jointed appendage.
explanations.C: Correct. Arthropods (insects, arachnids, crustaceans) are characterised by paired, jointed (articulated) appendages attached to a segmented body with an external chitinous exoskeleton. The defining structural feature of the phylum.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Nematodes (roundworms) are unsegmented, cylindrical worms with no limbs or appendages of any kind.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Cestodes (tapeworms) are flattened, segmented worms with a scolex bearing suckers (and sometimes hooks) for attachment, but no jointed appendages.

questions.learning_objective: Identify jointed (articulated) appendages as the defining feature of arthropods.

questions.title: Relationship where one benefits and the other is unharmed (Final 40)
questions.question: Which of the following is a relationship between two living organisms From which one benefits and the other is not harmed?

explanations.A: Incorrect. In parasitism the parasite benefits at the direct expense of the host, which is harmed; the stem specifies the other organism is not harmed, ruling out parasitism.
explanations.B: Correct. Commensalism is a relationship in which one organism benefits while the host is neither helped nor harmed. Exactly the relationship described.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Mutualism requires both partners to benefit; the stem specifies that only one organism benefits while the other is simply unharmed (not itself gaining), which does not fit mutualism.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Symbiosis is the broad umbrella term for organisms living together in close association, covering mutualism, commensalism and parasitism as subtypes; it is not itself the specific 'one benefits, other unharmed' relationship asked for.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Encystation is the process by which a protozoan forms a resistant cyst wall around itself, an unrelated concept describing a life-cycle stage transition rather than a relationship between two organisms.

questions.learning_objective: Define commensalism as a relationship in which one organism benefits and the other is unharmed.

questions.title: Host harbouring larval stage (Final 40)
questions.question: Which of the following is the host which harbours larval stage of parasite?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The definitive (final) host harbours the parasite's adult or sexual reproductive stage, not its larval stage.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A reservoir host is a non-human animal harbouring the same parasite species that infects humans, serving as an additional source of infection — a role defined by being an alternative infection source, not by hosting larval development.
explanations.C: Correct. The intermediate host is where all of the parasite's larval developmental stages take place. Active development occurs there before the parasite becomes infective for the next host in the cycle. This distinguishes it from a paratenic host, in which no further development occurs.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A vector is an arthropod that actively transmits a parasite between hosts, a transmission role rather than the specific site of larval development being asked for.
explanations.E: Incorrect. A paratenic host carries the parasite in an arrested state of development, with no further larval development occurring there, unlike the intermediate host where active development takes place.

questions.subtopic: Host types in the parasite life cycle
questions.learning_objective: Identify the intermediate host as the site of larval-stage development.

questions.title: Parasite transmitted by autoinfection
questions.question: Which of the following parasites can be transmitted by autoinfection?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ancylostoma duodenale (hookworm) eggs require a period of maturation in soil before larvae become infective by skin penetration; there is no autoinfection route in its life cycle.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Ascaris lumbricoides eggs must embryonate in soil for one to several weeks before becoming infective by ingestion; the parasite has no autoinfection cycle.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Trichuris trichiura eggs likewise require soil maturation before becoming infective by ingestion; there is no direct person-to-self reinfection route.
explanations.D: Correct. Enterobius vermicularis (the pinworm) is classically transmitted by autoinfection. The gravid female migrates out of the anus at night to lay eggs on the perianal skin, causing itching, and scratching contaminates the fingers with infective eggs that are transferred back to the mouth, re-establishing infection in the same host. This direct route, without needing to leave the body or mature in soil, is distinctive to Enterobius among the common intestinal nematodes.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Fasciola hepatica requires a snail intermediate host and encystment as metacercariae on aquatic vegetation before humans become infected by ingestion; it has no autoinfection cycle.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Enterobius vermicularis as transmitted by autoinfection via perianal egg contamination.

questions.title: Cause of bowel obstruction with a 20 cm passed worm
questions.question: Mother reported passage of a white worm of around 20 cm length with stool one week ago. He complained of diffuse abdominal pain, progressive food intolerance and vomiting. The child's weight and height were lower than expected for his age. He was irritable, dehydrated, had tachycardia, bloating, without bowel sounds. Palpable mass was detected in the right iliac fossa. Laboratory investigations showed eosinophilia of 10%. The abdominal radiograph showed bowel obstruction data, with multiple air-fluid levels, and a whirlpool image in the right iliac fossa. Which of the following organisms is the cause of this condition?

explanations.A: Correct. A large (up to 20-35 cm) roundworm passed in stool, together with eosinophilia, a palpable right iliac fossa mass, and radiographic bowel obstruction with a whirlpool sign, is the classic presentation of Ascaris lumbricoides causing mechanical intestinal obstruction. A heavy worm burden can twist into a tangled bolus large enough to occlude the narrow lumen of the small bowel. This complication is most often seen in heavily infected children, who tend to carry the heaviest worm burdens and have a narrower bowel lumen to begin with.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Diphyllobothrium latum is a much longer (several metres), flat, segmented tapeworm passed as ribbon-like proglottid chains, not as a single 20 cm round worm, and it classically causes vitamin B12 deficiency/megaloblastic anaemia rather than mechanical bowel obstruction.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Enterobius vermicularis is a small (about 1 cm) pinworm causing perianal itching, far too small to match a 20 cm passed worm or to cause bowel obstruction from worm bulk.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Taenia saginata sheds flat, segmented gravid proglottids, not a single smooth 20 cm round worm, and its typical presentation is mild gastrointestinal upset or asymptomatic passage of segments rather than bowel obstruction with a whirlpool sign.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Taenia solium likewise sheds flat, segmented proglottids rather than presenting as a single round worm, and its major clinical concern is neurocysticercosis from larval migration, not mechanical bowel obstruction from adult worm bulk.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise Ascaris lumbricoides as the cause of mechanical bowel obstruction from a large worm burden.

field_notes.relettered: source PDF prints options a,B,[c missing],d,[e missing] with the c/e labels dropped; relettered A-E in the printed order (Ascaris, D.latum, Enterobius, T.saginata, T.solium).

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: Best drug for Ascaris-related bowel obstruction
questions.question: Continuing the same case (20 cm worm passed, bowel obstruction with a whirlpool sign, confirmed as Ascaris lumbricoides): Which of the following is the best drug for treatment?

explanations.A: Correct. Mebendazole, a benzimidazole antihelminthic, is a standard first-line drug for treating ascariasis. It binds parasite beta-tubulin, blocking microtubule polymerisation and glucose uptake in the worm. This mechanism is selectively toxic to the helminth's cells while sparing the host.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Metronidazole is an antiprotozoal (and antianaerobic-bacterial) agent with no activity against roundworms such as Ascaris lumbricoides.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Niclosamide is directed at cestodes (tapeworms), inhibiting oxidative phosphorylation in the scolex and proximal segments; it has no established role against nematodes like Ascaris.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Praziquantel is effective against cestodes and trematodes by disrupting calcium homeostasis in the worm's tegument, but it is not an effective treatment for nematode infections such as ascariasis.

questions.learning_objective: Identify mebendazole as first-line treatment for ascariasis.

questions.title: Vector for Dipylidium caninum
questions.question: A 17-month-old boy has small white active worms seen in his stool over a month, with mild diarrhea. Tapeworm proglottids resembling cucumber seeds, each with two genital pores (one on each lateral edge) and numerous egg capsules, were seen in his stool. He responded to a single oral dose of praziquantel. His family has had household pet dogs for several years. Which of the following insects is responsible for infection with this parasite?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Anopheles mosquitoes are the vector of human malaria, playing no role in the Dipylidium caninum life cycle, which requires a flea rather than a mosquito.
explanations.B: Correct. Dipylidium caninum, the double-pored dog tapeworm. Matching this vignette's cucumber-seed proglottids with paired lateral genital pores and a dog-exposure history — uses the larval flea (dog or cat flea) as its intermediate host; humans, typically young children in close contact with infested pets, become infected by accidentally swallowing an infected adult flea.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Simulium (blackfly) transmits Onchocerca volvulus (river blindness), not Dipylidium caninum, which requires a flea intermediate host.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Soft ticks transmit organisms such as Borrelia (tick-borne relapsing fever), not Dipylidium caninum, whose life cycle depends specifically on the flea.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Stomoxys (stable fly) is a mechanical vector for some trypanosomes and can transmit Habronema in animals, but it plays no role in the Dipylidium caninum life cycle, which requires the flea as its biological intermediate host.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the flea as the intermediate host and vector of Dipylidium caninum.

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: Parasite causing appendicitis as a complication
questions.question: Acute appendicitis may occur as a complication of infection with which one of the following parasites?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Heterophyes heterophyes is a small intestinal fluke whose recognised complications relate to intestinal mucosal irritation and, uncommonly, ectopic egg embolisation to the heart or brain — not mechanical obstruction of the appendix.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Hymenolepis nana is a small intestinal tapeworm capable of autoinfection; its complications are related to heavy intraluminal burden rather than to mechanical occlusion of the appendiceal lumen by worm bulk.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Necator americanus (hookworm) attaches to and feeds on the small intestinal mucosa, causing iron-deficiency anaemia through chronic blood loss, not appendiceal obstruction.
explanations.D: Correct. A migrating adult Ascaris lumbricoides worm can enter and mechanically obstruct the lumen of the vermiform appendix, precipitating acute appendicitis. A recognised surgical complication of ascariasis, alongside its better-known small bowel obstruction from a heavy worm bolus.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Ancylostoma duodenale (hookworm), like Necator, causes iron-deficiency anaemia through mucosal blood-feeding, not mechanical appendiceal obstruction.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise Ascaris lumbricoides as a cause of acute appendicitis through appendiceal lumen obstruction.

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: Fisherman with stroke-like weakness
questions.question: A 65-year-old fisherman was referred to the emergency room with weakness and inability to move his left arm and leg. Which of the following parasites is expected to cause this condition?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Dipylidium caninum is a dog/cat-associated tapeworm acquired by accidentally swallowing an infected flea; it has no recognised mechanism for causing focal neurological deficits, and this vignette's occupational fish exposure does not fit its transmission route.
explanations.B: Correct. Heterophyes heterophyes is normally acquired by eating raw or undercooked brackish-water fish, fitting this fisherman's occupational exposure. Occasionally its eggs penetrate the intestinal mucosa, enter the mesenteric venules, and embolise via the bloodstream to ectopic sites such as the brain, where they can produce focal neurological deficits mimicking a stroke.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Hymenolepis diminuta (the rat tapeworm) is acquired by accidentally ingesting an infected grain beetle, an exposure unrelated to fishing, and it has no recognised mechanism of ectopic embolisation causing stroke-like weakness.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Hymenolepis nana is acquired by ingesting eggs (or by autoinfection) rather than through fish exposure, and it has no recognised mechanism for ectopic embolisation to the brain causing focal weakness.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise Heterophyes heterophyes as a rare cause of stroke-like symptoms via ectopic egg embolisation, in a fish-exposure context.

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: Diagnosis by Stoll's technique
questions.question: Stoll's technique can be used in the diagnosis of infection by which of the following parasites?

explanations.A: Correct. Stoll's dilution egg-counting technique is a quantitative stool method used to estimate the intensity of infection with helminths that shed very large numbers of eggs. It works by diluting a weighed stool sample and counting eggs in a small aliquot to calculate eggs per gram of stool. Ascaris lumbricoides, with its especially heavy and reliable egg output, is the classic organism for which this technique is used.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Capillaria philippinensis has a comparatively low and irregular egg output, for which quantitative dilution counting is not the diagnostic method of choice; a concentration technique is preferred instead.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Fasciola gigantica eggs are shed in relatively lower numbers than Ascaris and are typically detected by sedimentation concentration techniques, not by Stoll's quantitative dilution counting.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Heterophyes heterophyes eggs are small and shed in modest numbers, better suited to concentration methods (such as formol-ether sedimentation) than to Stoll's quantitative technique, which is intended for heavy-output helminths.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Hymenolepis nana egg output, while sometimes substantial, is not the classic example used for Stoll's dilution counting; Ascaris lumbricoides is the textbook example due to its especially heavy and reliable egg output.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Ascaris lumbricoides as the classic organism diagnosed by Stoll's quantitative egg-counting technique.

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: Parasite causing appendicitis and intestinal obstruction
questions.question: Which one of the following parasites cause appendicitis and intestinal obstruction?

explanations.A: Correct. Ascaris lumbricoides is the classic parasite recognised to cause both complications together. A heavy worm burden can twist into a tangled bolus that mechanically obstructs the small intestine, and a migrating adult worm can separately enter and obstruct the appendiceal lumen, precipitating appendicitis. Both complications reflect the size and motility of the adult worm rather than any toxin or tissue-invasive mechanism.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Enterobius vermicularis is a small pinworm best known for perianal itching and, less commonly, migration into the appendix causing mild inflammation; it is not classically associated with mechanical bowel obstruction from worm bulk the way Ascaris is.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Diphyllobothrium latum's major clinical concern is vitamin B12 deficiency/megaloblastic anaemia from competing for the vitamin in the gut, not appendicitis or intestinal obstruction.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Trichuris trichiura (whipworm) causes chronic colitis and, in heavy infection, rectal prolapse, not appendicitis or mechanical small bowel obstruction from worm bulk.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Ancylostoma duodenale (hookworm) attaches to the small intestinal mucosa and causes iron-deficiency anaemia through blood loss, not appendicitis or intestinal obstruction.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise Ascaris lumbricoides as the parasite causing both appendicitis and mechanical intestinal obstruction.

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: Best treatment for Ascaris (appendicitis/obstruction case)
questions.question: Continuing the same case (parasite causing appendicitis and intestinal obstruction, i.e. Ascaris lumbricoides): Which one of the following is the best treatment of this parasite?

explanations.A: Correct. Nitazoxanide is a broad-spectrum antiparasitic (thiazolide) agent with documented efficacy against Ascaris lumbricoides. It interferes with the pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase pathway that the organism's anaerobic energy metabolism depends on. This broad-spectrum activity also extends to several other helminths and protozoa, distinguishing it from narrower-spectrum antiparasitic drugs.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Triclabendazole is directed specifically at Fasciola species (liver flukes), not at intestinal nematodes such as Ascaris lumbricoides.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Mebendazole is also an effective benzimidazole option against Ascaris lumbricoides, but it is not the option identified as correct in this case.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Praziquantel is effective against cestodes and trematodes by disrupting tegumental calcium handling; it has no established role against nematodes such as Ascaris lumbricoides.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Spiramycin is a macrolide antibiotic used for toxoplasmosis in pregnancy; it has no antihelminthic activity against Ascaris lumbricoides.

questions.learning_objective: Identify nitazoxanide as a broad-spectrum antiparasitic effective against Ascaris lumbricoides.

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: Treatment of vaginal trichomoniasis
questions.question: A 27-year-old married female is complaining of offensive frothy yellowish vaginal discharge associated with burning, painful micturition and severe vulvar itching for 3 days. There was no perianal itching at night. On examination, there was no arthropod infestation. Which one of the following drugs is suitable for treatment?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Bithionol is used to treat Fasciola hepatica (liver fluke) infection, not a protozoal vaginal infection presenting with frothy, malodorous discharge.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Ivermectin is an antiparasitic used for organisms such as Strongyloides, Onchocerca and scabies mites; it has no role in treating a protozoal vaginal infection like this.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Praziquantel is effective against cestodes and trematodes, not against a protozoan such as Trichomonas vaginalis, which this frothy yellowish-discharge presentation classically represents.
explanations.D: Correct. This presentation of frothy, malodorous, yellowish vaginal discharge with burning, dysuria and vulvar itching, and no perianal itching or arthropod infestation to suggest an alternative cause, is classic for Trichomonas vaginalis infection. First-line treatment is metronidazole, a 5-nitroimidazole active against the trophozoite. Both sexual partners typically require treatment to prevent reinfection.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Thiabendazole is an older antihelminthic largely superseded for cutaneous larva migrans/strongyloidiasis; it has no role in treating trichomoniasis, a protozoal infection.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise the classic presentation of Trichomonas vaginalis vaginitis and identify metronidazole as its treatment.

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: True statement about trichomoniasis
questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE about trichomoniasis?

options.A: Men often show symptoms while women do not.
options.C: It is sexually transmitted disease caused by protozoon
options.D: It is caused by Trichomonus Vaginalis cyst.
options.E: Stool analysis helps in its diagnosis.

explanations.A: Incorrect. The pattern is generally the reverse — women are more often symptomatic (with vaginal discharge and irritation) while infection in men is frequently asymptomatic or under-recognised, not the other way around.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Trichomoniasis is a curable infection; metronidazole (or another 5-nitroimidazole) reliably clears Trichomonas vaginalis trophozoites in the great majority of cases.
explanations.C: Correct. Trichomoniasis is a curable sexually transmitted disease caused by the flagellated protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis. The organism exists only as a trophozoite, with no cyst stage in its life cycle. Diagnosis typically relies on examining vaginal or urethral secretions for motile trophozoites, not on stool examination.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Trichomonas vaginalis has no cyst stage at all; it exists only as a trophozoite, so a 'cyst' cannot be the infective or causative form.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Trichomonas vaginalis does not inhabit the gastrointestinal tract, so stool analysis plays no role in its diagnosis; diagnosis instead relies on examining vaginal/urethral secretions for motile trophozoites.

questions.learning_objective: Classify trichomoniasis as a curable, sexually transmitted protozoal infection with no cyst stage.

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: Characteristic lesion of scabies
questions.question: Which of the following is the most characteristic lesion of scabies?

explanations.A: Incorrect. A fissure is a linear skin crack seen in various dry or chronically irritated skin conditions; it is not a specific or characteristic finding of scabies.
explanations.B: Correct. The burrow is the most characteristic and specific skin lesion of scabies. It is a thin, greyish, thread-like tunnel produced by the female Sarcoptes scabiei mite as it tunnels through the epidermis to lay eggs, typically found in the finger web spaces and wrists. Other findings such as papules or vesicles can accompany scabies but are non-specific and seen in many other skin conditions.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Papules can accompany scabies as a secondary inflammatory response but are non-specific, appearing in many other skin conditions; they are not the pathognomonic scabies finding.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Vesicles can occasionally be seen in scabies, especially in infants, but are non-specific and seen in numerous other dermatoses, unlike the burrow.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Blisters are not a characteristic feature of scabies at all; they suggest an alternative diagnosis such as a bullous skin disorder or an insect-bite reaction.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the burrow as the pathognomonic lesion of scabies.

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: Confirming a scabies diagnosis
questions.question: A female patient aged 15 years old is complaining of severe itching between the fingers and wrist, increased at sleeping time. On examination, there were rashes and interdigital tortuous grayish tunnels. There were scratching marks and secondary bacterial infection over the lesions. Which of the following methods is the most likely to confirm the diagnosis?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Scabies is a localised ectoparasitic skin infestation; routine blood examination does not visualise the mite or its burrow and plays no role in confirming this diagnosis.
explanations.B: Correct. Dermoscopy is a non-invasive method that can confirm scabies by directly visualising the mite and its burrow. The mite itself is classically described as a small triangular structure, the 'delta-wing jet' sign, at the end of a burrow. This matches the interdigital tortuous grayish tunnels described in this vignette, without needing to physically extract the mite for microscopy.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Serological tests detect an antibody response and are not used to diagnose scabies, an ectoparasitic infestation confined to the skin surface rather than a systemic infection.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sarcoptes scabiei lives in the epidermis, not the gastrointestinal tract, so stool examination is irrelevant to diagnosing scabies.
explanations.E: Incorrect. An intradermal (delayed hypersensitivity) test is not a standard or useful method for confirming scabies, which is instead confirmed by direct visualisation of the mite or burrow.

questions.learning_objective: Identify dermoscopy as a method to confirm scabies by visualising the mite and burrow.

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: Probable diagnosis of pregnant patient's vaginal discharge
questions.question: A thirty two year old pregnant female came to her health care provider complaining of a frothy yellowish-green vaginal discharge, abnormal vaginal odour, vulva irritation, itching and dyspareunia. She gave a history of repeated use of vaginal disinfectants. What is your probable diagnosis?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Toxoplasmosis is typically asymptomatic or presents with mild lymphadenopathy in immunocompetent adults; it does not cause a frothy, malodorous vaginal discharge.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Leishmaniasis presents as cutaneous, mucocutaneous or visceral disease depending on species, not as vaginal discharge.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Trypanosomiasis presents as a systemic febrile illness (African sleeping sickness or Chagas disease), not as localised vaginal discharge.
explanations.D: Correct. A frothy, malodorous, yellowish-green vaginal discharge with vulvar irritation, itching and dyspareunia is the classic presentation of Trichomonas vaginalis infection (trichomoniasis). This presentation is a common cause of vaginal discharge in sexually active women, including during pregnancy. Recognising it guides both diagnostic testing and treatment choice.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Toxocariasis presents as visceral or ocular larva migrans from an accidental dog/cat roundworm infection, not as vaginal discharge.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise the classic frothy, malodorous discharge of Trichomonas vaginalis infection.

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: Mode of infection with Trichomonas vaginalis
questions.question: Continuing the same pregnant patient's case (Trichomonas vaginalis infection): What is the mode of infection of this parasite?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Trichomonas vaginalis has no cyst stage at all, so ingestion of a 'mature cyst' cannot be its mode of infection.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Trichomonas vaginalis is not acquired by ingesting a trophozoite; the fragile trophozoite instead spreads by direct genital contact or brief environmental contact via a moist fomite, not through the gastrointestinal route.
explanations.C: Incorrect. An oocyst is the environmentally resistant stage of organisms such as Toxoplasma gondii, not a stage in the Trichomonas vaginalis life cycle, which has no oocyst.
explanations.D: Correct. While its principal route is sexual contact, Trichomonas vaginalis trophozoites can survive briefly outside the body in a moist, warm environment. This allows non-sexual transmission by fomites such as shared damp or contaminated towels. The organism has no resistant cyst stage, so this fomite spread depends on the fragile trophozoite surviving briefly in a favourable environment rather than on ingesting any resistant form.
explanations.E: Incorrect. A pseudocyst is a tissue-cyst-like stage seen in Toxoplasma gondii bradyzoites, not a stage in the Trichomonas vaginalis life cycle.

questions.learning_objective: State that Trichomonas vaginalis, lacking a cyst stage, can spread non-sexually via fomites such as contaminated towels.

questions.source_citation: Parasitology Past Exams - MCQ Answers - Telegram 9673.pdf, p.{page} (V.I.P Questions)
questions.title: Cause of dyspnea via inhalant allergy
questions.question: Which of the following can be a cause of dyspnea through an allergic (inhalant) mechanism rather than tissue invasion?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Strongyloides larvae migrating through the lungs (Loeffler-type pneumonitis) can cause dyspnea, but through direct larval tissue migration and eosinophilic inflammation, not through an inhalant allergic mechanism.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Schistosomiasis can cause pulmonary symptoms through acute (Katayama) hypersensitivity to migrating schistosomula or through chronic egg-induced pulmonary hypertension, both tissue-based mechanisms rather than inhalant allergy.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) causes perianal itching and does not have a recognised pulmonary migration phase or mechanism causing dyspnea.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Paragonimus (lung fluke) causes dyspnea and haemoptysis through direct parenchymal and pleural tissue invasion and cyst formation in the lung, not through an inhalant allergic mechanism.
explanations.E: Correct. House dust mites are a major perennial inhalant allergen. Their faecal particles and body fragments trigger IgE-mediated allergic reactions in sensitised individuals, presenting as allergic rhinitis and allergic asthma with dyspnea and wheeze. This allergic mechanism is entirely distinct from the tissue-invasive or migratory mechanisms by which helminths and flukes can cause respiratory symptoms.

questions.learning_objective: Identify house dust mites as a cause of dyspnea through an IgE-mediated inhalant allergic mechanism.

Printed key (E, Dust mites) kept as-is.
